Assignment 04 / Sculpting for Design

Wire Sculpture

I used bent and wrapped wire to explore a dinosaur’s volume and a dancer’s gesture.

Wire · Volume · Gesture

For the animal and human wire forms, I chose a brachiosaurus and a dancer. I worked between a densely wrapped body and a more open, gestural figure.

01

Thinking through a line

I tested possible structures through drawings, including repeated loops, enclosed volumes, a figure in motion, and an animal with a long neck.

My sketches helped me think about the body, limbs, and overall pose before bending the wire. I was moving from a line that describes an outline on paper to one that has to hold its shape in space.

02

Building a brachiosaurus

I wanted to make a brachiosaurus, a herbivorous dinosaur. I used overlapping lengths of wire to establish its torso, with a long neck, projecting head, and four legs giving the piece its silhouette.

I wrapped wire around the body to build volume while leaving gaps between the strands. The photographs show how the piece reads as a substantial form while still revealing its construction.

03

A familiar movement

For my human figure, I returned to Mohiniyattam, the Kerala dance form I have trained in for over ten years. I wanted to make a dancer and connect the material exercise with a practice I know through movement.

I used the raised arm and bent limbs to make the pose readable with relatively little material. Compared with the densely wrapped dinosaur, my dancer relies more on an open outline and the relationship between the limbs.

04

Two ways to occupy space

I explored two ways of occupying space with the same material. I built up the dinosaur into a rounded body, while using a more economical structure to describe the dancer’s pose.

The project connected my observations of an animal’s proportions with my own experience of a dancer’s gesture.
